items.hed: The Houston Texans dominated the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 on Thursday Night Football at NRG Stadium, with C.J. Stroud throwing three touchdown passes as Houston heads into Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens
items.insight: Stroud threw for 194 yards and three touchdowns — to Nico Collins, Kayson Boutte and Marlin Klein — as Houston built an early lead and never trailed, with defensive end Logan Hall blocking a 62-yard field goal try and the defense holding Indianapolis without a touchdown for the first time since 2024. Head coach DeMeco Ryans had told the team all week the home fans deserved a win at NRG Stadium, and linebacker Will Anderson Jr. set the tone defensively, drawing praise from Stroud and even the Colts' own coaching staff. The Texans now turn to Sunday's matchup with the Ravens, with the team's own site carrying full broadcast and streaming information.
items.image_caption: NRG Stadium (formerly Reliant Stadium), Houston. Venue still.

items.hed: New Astros general manager Randy Flores began reshaping Houston's outfield this week, outrighting Joey Loperfido to Triple-A and non-tendering Taylor Trammell after the unit posted the majors' 29th-ranked .662 OPS last season
items.insight: The team's own site reports Flores, in one of his first major roster moves, outrighted Loperfido to Triple-A Sugar Land on Nov. 17 while adding right-hander Jackson Nezuh to the 40-man roster to protect him from the Rule 5 Draft, then non-tendered outfielder Taylor Trammell on Friday. The moves follow Flores and new manager Brad Ausmus filling out the front office and coaching staff this month, including hiring Bobby Wilson as bench coach and Matt Bayer as an assistant general manager, as Houston works through an offseason overhaul aimed at fixing the outfield production that lagged the rest of the roster in 2026.
items.image_caption: Daikin Park (formerly Minute Maid Park), 2010. Venue still.

items.hed: The Houston Rockets fell to the Denver Nuggets 133-124 in Denver on Friday night in Emirates NBA Cup West Group A play, a rematch loss after Houston had beaten Denver earlier this month
items.insight: The Rockets dropped Friday's game at Ball Arena after winning the season's earlier meeting between the two teams, splitting the season series ahead of any further Cup or regular-season matchups, according to the NBA's own schedule and box-score pages. The loss counts in both NBA Cup West Group A standings and the regular-season column, and comes in the middle of a road-heavy stretch of Houston's schedule. The Rockets' next games are available on the league's official schedule page; Texas viewers should check the NBA's own broadcast listing rather than unofficial streams.
